//: Branch protection on main requires a branch to be current before it merges (strict). Without this, every Renovate pull request goes stale the moment anything else lands and has to be rebased by hand.
//prConcurrentLimit: Twelve charts, a Go module graph and the pinned actions all become due at once on the first run. A flood of pull requests is a flood nobody reads.
//schedule: Batched weekly. Chart upgrades are read, not merged on sight, so they should arrive when somebody is going to look at them.

vulnerabilityAlerts.//: Security fixes ignore the schedule and the concurrency limit.

customManagers.//: Chart pins live in Go, not in a Chart.yaml, so no built-in manager sees them. The pattern keys off the field order Name → Repo → Version, which every entry in the registry follows; a test in tools/charts reads this very regex out of this file and asserts it still matches every chart, because the failure mode otherwise is Renovate silently opening no pull requests at all.

packageRules.//: A chart upgrade changes what this repository deploys, so it belongs in a release. semantic-release cuts a patch from fix and a minor from feat, which puts a major chart jump in the version rather than hiding it.

AppVersion beside each pin cannot be maintained by a bot: the helm datasource knows chart versions and nothing else. `task charts:appversions` fails these pull requests until a human sets it, which is also when the changelog gets read.
prBodyNotes: `AppVersion` in `pkg/charts/registry.go` is **not** updated by this pull request and the `Chart pins` check will fail until it is.
Run `task charts:appversions` for the value to set, and update the `// app <version>` comment beside `Version` to match.

packageRules.//: Tooling and the module graph are not deployable changes, so chore keeps them out of the release notes.
One pull request for the Go module graph's routine moves. Individually they are noise; together they are one review.
Actions are pinned to commit shas with a version comment; Renovate maintains both.
